A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Blink research work. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and complete supplementary materials are readable and support reliable matching across relocations and renumbering.

before.justification: V1 reports original LLaVA-1.5 and LLaVA-NeXT benchmark results, component and configuration ablations, and attention analyses.

after.justification: V2 retains those experiments and adds original Qwen2.5-VL-7B results and a reproduced ViCrop comparison with resource-cost reporting.

M1.justification: Section 3 and Algorithm 1 retain the same saliency calculation, expansion/drop procedure, TokenSR architecture, and training objective. Appendix A.2 clarifies spatially matched, interpolated training inputs already described in v1; it does not establish a procedural change.

E1.justification: The training datasets and seven evaluation benchmarks are retained. The added Qwen2.5-VL and ViCrop experiments reuse MME, GQA, POPE, and ScienceQA coverage; they introduce model/comparator configurations rather than new datasets or task scenarios.

E2.justification: V1 compares vanilla backbones with Blink and its variants. V2 Appendix D/Table 7 adds reproduced ViCrop on LLaVA-1.5-7B across MME, GQA, and POPE, introducing the first evaluated competing perception-enhancement method rather than merely citing it.

E3.justification: V2 adds Qwen2.5-VL-7B as an evaluation configuration and introduces theoretical maximum FLOPs per image, full forward-pass counts, and FP16 memory reporting. It does not report revised protocols for the retained benchmark experiments.

E4.justification: Appendix D adds an overhead analysis: Blink requires 9.73T versus ViCrop's 21.5T FLOPs and one versus three forward passes; GPU memory is reported as 20.8 GB versus vanilla's 19.7 GB. Existing component, threshold, layer-range, patch-count, interpolation, and attention analyses remain unchanged.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The new results retain the existing point-estimate reporting practice.

E6.justification: V2 adds substantive backbone and competitor result sets while retaining every original table entry. Table 6 reports Qwen2.5-VL Blink/vanilla MME cognition scores of 608.57/598.57. Table 7 reports Blink/ViCrop scores of 1881.53/1804.65 on MME, 61.98/60.98 on GQA, and 85.23/87.25 on POPE, alongside new efficiency results. These are additional comparisons, not improvements over v1 under changed backbones.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions and Equations 1–6 are unchanged, as is the appendix's patch-dependent threshold scaling. Neither version adds formal propositions or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's contribution statements, and conclusion retain the same claims about attention shifts, computation on salient regions, and dynamic visual-token resolution within one forward pass. The added evaluations support those existing claims.

C2.justification: Appendices C.2 and D add interpretations concerning generality to modern backbones and practical performance-efficiency tradeoffs, including an inferred latency benefit. Existing mechanism explanations and the convolutional-design and model-size limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: V2 removes v1 Appendix C's explicit LLaVA-NeXT layer ranges and expansion/drop thresholds, reducing reproducibility information for retained results. It newly specifies FP16 for memory reporting. Shared training hyperparameters, hardware, and software details remain unchanged.

R1.justification: The same 52 cited works remain; reference edits primarily update bibliographic metadata. Appendix D adds explicit performance and efficiency positioning against the already-cited ViCrop, extending v1's qualitative discussion of competing approaches.

P1.justification: V2 locally condenses Sections 4.4–4.5 and related-work prose, clarifies Appendix A.2, subdivides Appendix C, and inserts the ViCrop section. It also revises affiliation/footnote text and adds acknowledgements. The overall narrative and most wording remain intact.

P2.justification: V2 adds Qwen2.5-VL and ViCrop Tables 6–7; the existing patch and interpolation tables become Tables 8–9. Several displays move or become more compact, including Table 3 and Figures 6–7, and some captions are shortened. All original figure image content is retained.

improvement.justification: The additional model family and first direct competing-method comparison strengthen empirical support beyond v1, while resource reporting makes efficiency claims more assessable. The gain is limited by omitted Qwen-specific settings, removed LLaVA-NeXT settings, and overbroad interpretation: Table 7 favors ViCrop on POPE, and the claimed latency benefit lacks reported timings. These weaknesses temper the useful additional evidence.
